title: Regression shepherding and heterogeneous-deployment mediation for model rollouts
creator: Anika Shah
description: When a model rollout exhibits asymmetric regressions between Hosted, Dedicated and Private planes we need a defined, low-friction process to shepherd the regression to resolution while minimizing customer impact. This ticket creates a mediation pattern ("shepherd") and operational checklist for cross-environment incidents where behavior diverges, including tenant-scoped fixes, KV/prefix cache reconciliation, model-variant pin handshakes, and targeted rollback coordination. The goal is to shorten mean time to containment (MTC) and reduce noisy tenant escalations by providing a predictable choreography for engineers, support, and field liaisons.
acceptance_criteria: A documented mediation checklist is merged into the runbooks Confluence page with step-by-step actions for Hosted/Dedicated/Private divergence
A small automation (Lambda/Runbook job) exists to snapshot routing, model pins, and KV cache versions for a tenant slice within 60s
Playbook includes tenant-priority matrix and explicit communication templates for field & support
A runbook test run was executed in staging: simulated cross-env divergence and verified rollback handshake and KV reconciliation steps
On-call and SRE have signed off on the rollback safety checks and rate-limited unpin flow
implementation_notes: Design a 'shepherd token' payload that travels with a rollout request and records model-variant, routing-tier, KV-cache-hash, and origin-plane
Add a small API endpoint (/v1/rollback-handshake) on the admin plane for safe pin/unpin with 2-step validation for Dedicated/Private tenants
KV reconciliation step: provide idempotent rehydrate job that can reapply prefix caches for a tenant slice after rollback; include checksums to avoid stale overwrites
Fallback policy: prefer model-variant pin over immediate cross-plane rollback when 1) only quality degradation and 2) affected traffic < 5% of tenant SLA band
Telemetry: capture model-output-sig deviation metric per tenant and raise automatic P0 if deviation > configured threshold for > 10m
testing_plan: Unit tests for handshake endpoint and token payload validation
Integration test that simulates a model variant returning altered tokenization to validate checksum detection
Chaos test in staging: apply transient KV drift to a tenant slice and verify rehydrate job restores expected response signatures
Red-team runbook drill with SRE + Support: simulate a high-severity customer escalation and exercise communication templates
rollout_playbook: Step 1 - Triage: collect shepherd token, tenant slice ID, routing tier, model-variant, and KV-cache-hash. Post to #prod-escalations with required fields
Step 2 - Contain: shadow-traffic reroute to a safe variant if available; if not, apply model pin for affected tenants using /v1/rollback-handshake with 'dry-run' validation
Step 3 - Reconcile: run KV rehydrate job for affected tenant slice and validate checksums and sample outputs via the diagnostic endpoint
Step 4 - Patch: if regression is code-related, open a hotfix branch, attach repro payloads and sample outputs; if model-related, coordinate with model-onboarding to rollback or redeploy variant
Step 5 - Communicate: update customer liaison doc + send templated status updates to customers and internal stakeholders every 30 minutes until containment
Step 6 - Postmortem: publish a short incident finding with root cause, what worked, and action items within 3 business days
